title: I built a classic-inspired browser MMO in pure TypeScript with no game engine. Here’s what I learned.
author: GastonSaillen
selftext:
I’m a software engineer based in Argentina with zero experience in game development.

Two months ago, I was hit by an obsession: can you build a browser-based MMO in the spirit of classic MU Online, Diablo, and WoW, using pure TypeScript and rendering libraries—no Unity, Unreal, or Godot?

I initially assumed AI tools would carry most of the weight. I was dead wrong. While AI sped up some boilerplate, building a game without a engine meant solving every low-level problem manually: browser performance limits, raw shader compilation, asset loading, and strict memory management. Getting smooth, playable performance was a grueling fight.

On top of that, I’m not a 3D artist. Putting together basic models in Blender and engineering a dynamic modular armor system (so gear swaps reflect on your character) took weeks of trial and error, and it’s still rough around the edges.

**Where the playable alpha stands today (\~10h of content):**

* Questlines, mob farming, and a gear item-refining system (+1 to +9).
* Shared open-world boss fights.
* Full multiplayer infrastructure: parties, direct trading, friend lists, and talent trees.
* 2 classes and 16 unique armor sets.

The server is hosted in São Paulo. Because of how state updates are handled, latency is imperceptible even outside South America. If interest grows, I’ll spin up regional nodes elsewhere.

My vision for **Velundra** is to gradually turn it into a home for players who miss the golden era of old-school ARPGs and MMOs. It’s easily the most demanding project I’ve ever tackled—I've barely slept 5 hours a night for the past two months.

It’s completely free and runs straight in the browser: [**velundra.io**](http://velundra.io)

Brutal feedback is welcome—the link to the Discord is on the site. Also, if anyone wants to collaborate (3D assets, animation, audio, or code), hit me up!

Thanks for reading! 🙏

comments.body:
I’d kill to know your tools, workflow or any tips you have for the gear swapping with consistent animations. Especially robes.   
I’ve been trying to use Mixamo rigs and animations to capture and create 2d spite animation pages for my turn based rpg but I’m lost on how to build the clean gear swaps you have.   
Especially with the cloth movement. It looks great, nice work!
